A.support: Actual Masoretic qere supplies beneficiary to-it, with the preceding singular nation a coherent antecedent. Both growth and increased joy match immediately following rejoicing/harvest/spoil and the three explanatory for clauses about deliverance, destroyed war gear and the child. This is contextual source fidelity, not merely smoother English.
A.objection: Qere may be a contextual repair of an older difficult negative; writtennegative and selectedLatin are genuine contrary evidence. Ancient1QIsa-a spelling cannot independently confirm the affirmative sense. Context alone does not prove autograph priority.

B.support: Direct written Masoretic negative and selectedLatinnegative are actually attested; difficult reading need not be an error. A contrast between prior expansion without joy and later rejoicing is possible within the broader darkness/deliverance passage.
B.objection: Current unqualified negative clause interrupts the opening light/deliverance movement and immediate rejoicing. A prior-period, relative-clause or rhetorical-question repair needs an unexpressed relation; the text does not expressly mark that transition in this colon. Difficulty alone does not establish priority.

root_assessment.transmission: Similar sounding written/read forms and Qumran spelling neutrality leave both corruption/interchange and contextual reading-repair plausible. No scribal motive, directional proof or witness-count argument is asserted.
root_assessment.chronology: The earlier direct Hebrew form is semantically nondiscriminating; no chronological tie-breaker selects either sense. Modern edition release dates are not manuscript dates.
root_assessment.working_preference: Propose A as a provisional qere-based source/English application, preserving writtennegative and Latin evidence in the apparatus/note. This is not an English-only edit against the current negative source.
root_assessment.other_candidate: Do not adopt conjectural haggilah or combine Greek first-colon wording with the selected Masoretic form.

independent_candidate_assessment.verdict: Propose A as working source preference with moderate confidence; earliest wording not established; B remains substantial attested alternative.
independent_candidate_assessment.actual_assessment: A follows the recorded qere with the singular nation as beneficiary; its restoration clauses fit the immediate harvest/victory rejoicing and subsequent explanatory clauses. Its objection is that it may smooth an older negative. B directly renders the written negative and selected Latin; difficulty does not disqualify it. Its objection is an abrupt denial of increased joy within relief/light/celebration, with prior-time or referent shifts unstated. Same-scroll uses show both meanings of לוא; age cannot decide. 4Q57 begins the following verse. Greek opening and 'your joy' differ from the qere construction and cannot recover exact לו. Latin is clear contrary versional evidence, not a Hebrew exemplar. The NET conjecture is distinct from the actual qere, and its 'obviously incorrect' judgment is not adopted. B accurately renders its negative source; A requires explicit source selection, not English-only polishing.
independent_candidate_assessment.scope: One bounded source/English comparison; no exact full-record application, publication, historical certainty or canon approval.

decision.main_english_proposal: You have multiplied the nation; you have increased its joy. They rejoice before you as with the joy at harvest, as men exult when they divide spoil.
